children.prompt: Prove that there is no closed knight’s tour on a $5\times5$ chess board.

answer.short:
No closed knight’s tour exists.

Each move changes square colour, so a closed tour must visit equal numbers of each colour. A $5\times5$ board has 13 squares of one colour and 12 of the other.
answer.worked:
Suppose a closed knight’s tour exists on a $5\times5$ chessboard. Every knight move changes square colour. Since the route returns to its starting square, its visited squares alternate colours cyclically, so it must visit equal numbers of squares of each colour.

The board has 13 squares of one colour and 12 of the other. A tour visiting every square exactly once would therefore visit unequal numbers of the two colours, a contradiction. Hence no closed knight’s tour exists.
